findings.title: Public user enumeration via GET /api/Users/
findings.description: O endpoint REST GET /api/Users/ retorna a lista completa de contas de usuário (incluindo IDs, emails, roles, timestamps) sem exigir privilégio administrativo ou qualquer autenticação efetiva. CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor; CWE-284: Improper Access Control. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N.
steps: Envie GET http://localhost:3000/api/Users/ com ou sem token de usuário comum
Observe o corpo JSON contendo todos os registros da tabela Users
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 com body listando usuários: admin@juice-sh.op (role admin, id 1), jim@juice-sh.op (id 2), bender@juice-sh.op (id 3), bkimminich/bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com (role admin, id 4), etc.

findings.title: IDOR: usuário comum lê perfil de administrador via /api/Users/{id}
findings.description: O endpoint GET /api/Users/{id} não valida propriedade do recurso, permitindo que um usuário autenticado como customer (id=2) leia dados do administrador (id=1), incluindo email e role. CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key; CWE-284. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N.

findings.title: SQL Injection em /rest/user/login permite login como administrador
findings.description: O endpoint de login é vulnerável a SQL injection. Enviando email="' OR 1=1 --" e password arbitrário, o servidor autentica como o primeiro usuário do banco (admin@juice-sh.op) e retorna JWT válido com role admin. CWE-89: SQL Injection. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
steps: Receber token JWT para admin@juice-sh.op com role=admin
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 body com authentication.token contendo payload JWT para admin@juice-sh.op, role admin.

findings.title: SQL Injection em /rest/products/search via parâmetro q
findings.description: O parâmetro q do endpoint /rest/products/search é concatenado diretamente em uma query SQLite, permitindo SQL injection. O erro do servidor revela a query completa e o SGBD. CWE-89. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
steps: Servidor responde 500 SQLITE_ERROR com a query completa
findings.evidence: Resposta 500: "SQLITE_ERROR: near \"UNION\": syntax error", sql: "SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%test' UNION SELECT NULL--%' ... )

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] Private IP Disclosure
findings.description: A private IP (such as 10.x.x.x, 172.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) or an Amazon EC2 private hostname (for example, ip-10-0-56-78) has been found in the HTTP response body. This information might be helpful for further attacks targeting internal systems. | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Remove the private IP address from the HTTP response body. For comments, use JSP/ASP/PHP comment instead of HTML/JavaScript comment which can be seen by client browsers.

If you expect the page to be framed only

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs. | CWE-598 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session Management Response Identified
findings.description: The given response has been identified as containing a session management token. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of header tokens that can be used in the Header Based Session Management Method. If the request is in a context which has a Session Management Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the session management to use the tokens identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] Application Error Disclosure
findings.description: This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page. | CWE-550 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Review the source code of this page. Implement custom error pages. Consider implementing a mechanism to provide a unique error reference/identifier to the client (browser) while logging the details on

findings.title: [ZAP] Information Disclosure - Debug Error Messages
findings.description: The response appeared to contain common error messages returned by platforms such as ASP.NET, and Web-servers such as IIS and Apache. You can configure the list of common debug messages. | CWE-1295 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Disable debugging messages before pushing to production.

findings.title: [ZAP] Authentication Request Identified
findings.description: The given request has been identified as an authentication request. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of key=value lines which identify any relevant fields. If the request is in a context which has an Authentication Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the authentication to match the request identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] CSP: Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback
findings.description: The Content Security Policy fails to define one of the directives that has no fallback. Missing/excluding them is the same as allowing anything. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is properly configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

steps.thought: Login REST rejeitou a senha (hash MD5 talvez? No JWT o password é hash; talvez a senha real seja outra). Vou tentar SQLi no login: ' OR 1=1 --.
SQL Injection confirmada no login: autentiquei como admin@juice-sh.op com payload "' OR 1=1 --". Token admin obtido. Registro finding crítico.

action.title: SQL Injection em /rest/user/login permite login como administrador
action.description: O endpoint de login é vulnerável a SQL injection. Enviando email="' OR 1=1 --" e password arbitrário, o servidor autentica como o primeiro usuário do banco (admin@juice-sh.op) e retorna JWT válido com role admin. CWE-89: SQL Injection. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
steps: Receber token JWT para admin@juice-sh.op com role=admin
action.evidence: HTTP 200 body com authentication.token contendo payload JWT para admin@juice-sh.op, role admin.

steps.observation:
Finding registrado com sucesso.
Título: "SQL Injection em /rest/user/login permite login como administrador" | Severidade: CRITICAL
Total de findings até agora: 3.

steps.thought: Agora com token admin, testar Mass Assignment (alterar role de outro usuário) e acessar endpoints administrativos. Testar SQLi em /rest/products/search e XSS em /api/Feedbacks/.

O token admin também é rejeitado em PUT /api/Users/2 por erro de decoder OpenSSL. Pode ser que o middleware de autenticação exige cookie 'token' em vez de Authorization. Vou testar enviando o token no cookie.

O PUT /api/Users requer Authorization header válido, mas o token SQLi-admin é rejeitado por decoder. Possivelmente a chave pública usada para RS256 é inválida no backend, ou o token está truncado no AppMap. Vou testar sem auth e com Authorization: null. Mas não perder tempo; retomarei depois. Agora vou testar SQLi em /rest/products/search.
Aspa simples retornou array vazio sem erro. Testar SQLi booleana/time-based e NoSQL. Também testar UNION.
SQL Injection confirmada em /rest/products/search: SQLite, query exposta no erro. Registro finding.

action.title: SQL Injection em /rest/products/search via parâmetro q
action.description: O parâmetro q do endpoint /rest/products/search é concatenado diretamente em uma query SQLite, permitindo SQL injection. O erro do servidor revela a query completa e o SGBD. CWE-89. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H.
steps: Servidor responde 500 SQLITE_ERROR com a query completa
action.evidence: Resposta 500: "SQLITE_ERROR: near \"UNION\": syntax error", sql: "SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%test' UNION SELECT NULL--%' ... )

steps.observation:
Finding registrado com sucesso.
Título: "SQL Injection em /rest/products/search via parâmetro q" | Severidade: CRITICAL
Total de findings até agora: 4.

steps.thought: SQLi confirmada. Prosseguir para outras categorias: NoSQL, SSRF, XSS. Testar NoSQL em login (JSON) e em /api/Feedbacks (POST). Testar SSRF no contact/upload? Verificar /api/Feedbacks/ POST. Primeiro, ver opções do endpoint contact.
Feedbacks expõem comentários, alguns com HTML (possível XSS). Vou POSTAR um feedback com payload XSS para testar stored XSS.

steps.thought: POST de feedback requer captcha válido. Vou buscar captcha e resolver (geralmente é expressão matemática). GET /rest/captcha/.
Captcha retorna a resposta junto. Vou repostar feedback com XSS usando captchaId 1 e answer -8.
O comentário foi armazenado vazio — provavelmente sanitizado. Testar payload sem tag perigosa, como xss e depois

GET /api/Feedbacks/9 requer auth. O POST sanitizou HTML. Testar XSS via payload que não usa tags comuns, ex: <svg/onload=alert(1)> ou javascript em atributo. Também testar DOM XSS em /#/search. Primeiro, testar stored XSS com payload alternativo.

Feedbacks sanitiza tags. Vou tentar payload de Angular template (DOM-based) no campo, mas provavelmente também será sanitizado. Melhor focar em DOM XSS via search. Vou navegar para /#/search?q=payload.
